observations.text: SP executed the straight ahead rejoin to the block standard, completing the closure only with the IP directing the power reduction and executing part of the stabilization in route position. Airspeed settled 12 knots fast and altitude 80 feet above No1 level after the IP's inputs, and visual on No1 was kept throughout. Marginal performance for the Training Section; a self-initiated power correction based on Aspect Angle and Angle Off is expected on the next sortie.

SP completed the straight ahead rejoin according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual without the IP taking any part of the maneuver, correcting the closure after the IP's verbal indications. Airspeed in route position stabilized at the 15 knot limit and altitude at 100 feet from No1 level, with the deviations recognized and corrected with delay. Visual on No1 was continuously maintained. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew the straight ahead rejoin with smooth and solid A/C control and required no verbal indication from the IP. Minor errors in judging Angle Off produced 9 knots of excess airspeed in route position and 70 feet above No1 level, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the straight ahead rejoin accurately and rapidly according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual, remaining cognizant of Aspect Angle and Angle Off throughout the closure. Visual on No1 was continuous and stabilization in route position was achieved within 4 knots of airspeed and 30 feet of No1 level. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the straight ahead rejoin and the straight ahead tactical rejoin with exceptional precision, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid manner from the initial closure to route position. Deviations were negligible, with 2 knots of airspeed and 15 feet from No1 level, and visual on No1 was never interrupted. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a closure technique that delayed the power reduction beyond the point of maximum overtake, did not stabilize in route position on the straight ahead rejoin. Airspeed exceeded No1 by 22 knots and the A/C arrived 130 feet above No1 level, with the result that the IP directed the Overshoot and executed part of the deceleration.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not recognize the excessive Angle Off developing on the straight ahead rejoin and did not inform the formation leader timely that the overshoot was unavoidable. The A/C passed route position 20 knots fast and 120 feet above No1 level, with the result that the IP directed the Overshoot and initiated the separation. Further study of the rejoin geometry in the Techniques and Procedures Manual is required.

SP flew the straight ahead rejoin within the block standard, stabilizing in route position at the 15 knot and 100 foot limits only after the IP's verbal indications on the closure rate. Aspect Angle assessment was late on both rejoins and the corrections were applied with delay. Marginal performance for the Training Section; earlier power control based on Angle Off is expected to improve on the next sortie.

SP applied a more timely power reduction and flew the straight ahead rejoin with small errors in closure control that produced 8 knots of overtake in route position and 60 feet above No1 level. Both deviations were recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention, and visual on No1 was continuously maintained. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the straight ahead rejoin accurately and rapidly according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual, remaining cognizant of Aspect Angle and Angle Off from the initial acceleration to stabilization. Route position was held within 4 knots of airspeed and 25 feet of No1 level, and the straight ahead tactical rejoin was flown to the briefed geometry. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP demonstrated exceptional precision on both the straight ahead rejoin and the straight ahead tactical rejoin, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid manner throughout the closure. Airspeed in route position varied by no more than 2 knots and altitude by no more than 10 feet from No1 level, with visual on No1 never lost. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a rejoin entry flown with excessive power and without reference to the closure cues, did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid manner during the straight ahead rejoin. The A/C arrived at route position with 25 knots of overtake and 140 feet above No1 level, with the result that the IP took the controls and executed the Overshoot.

SP, due to a lack of assertiveness in voicing a recognized unsafe closure, did not inform the formation leader timely that the overshoot was unavoidable and did not execute the Break Out on his own initiative after losing visual contact with No1. Lateral separation reduced below the briefed value with 20 knots of overtake and 130 feet above No1 level, with the result that the IP directed the Break Out and flew the separation maneuver. Calling the overshoot before the closure becomes unmanageable requires further emphasis.

SP, due to a late assessment of Aspect Angle that delayed the power reduction, did not stabilize in route position on the first straight ahead rejoin without prompting. Airspeed settled at the 15 knot limit and altitude at 100 feet from No1 level, with the result that the corrections were completed only after the IP's verbal indications and were recognized with delay.

SP, due to inadequate workload management while flying the closure and working the formation frequency at the same time, did not keep the Angle Off within the values of the Techniques and Procedures Manual on the straight ahead rejoin. The A/C reached route position 15 knots fast and 100 feet above No1 level, with the result that stabilization was achieved only after the IP's verbal indications and the deviation was recognized with delay.

SP flew the straight ahead rejoin within the desired standards, keeping continuous visual on No1 and reaching route position with 12 knots of overtake and 70 feet above No1 level on the first attempt, both corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section; a more consistent early power reduction based on Aspect Angle is expected to reduce the residual overtake.

SP executed the straight ahead rejoin accurately and rapidly according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual, remaining cognizant of Aspect Angle and Angle Off throughout the closure. Route position was established within 3 knots of airspeed and 25 feet of No1 level without any verbal indication from the IP. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP flew both the straight ahead rejoin and the straight ahead tactical rejoin with exceptional precision, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid manner and keeping visual on No1 without interruption. Deviations in route position did not exceed 2 knots of airspeed and 15 feet from No1 level. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a closure flown without reference to the overtake cues of the Techniques and Procedures Manual, did not begin the power reduction at the prescribed range on the straight ahead rejoin. The A/C passed route position with 30 knots of overtake and 150 feet above No1 level, with the result that the IP took the controls and executed the Overshoot.

SP, due to a perceptual error in judging closure and lateral separation, did not maintain the Angle Off required to arrive at route position on the straight ahead rejoin. Visual contact with No1 was lost during the resulting Overshoot and no Break Out was initiated, with the result that the IP directed the separation and flew part of the recovery to formation. Overtake at the closest point was 25 knots with 140 feet of altitude split from No1 level. Further study of the rejoin geometry and of the Break Out criteria is required.

SP, due to a power reduction applied in a single large step instead of progressively, did not control the A/C in a smooth and solid manner during the straight ahead rejoin. Airspeed in route position reached the 15 knot limit and altitude 100 feet from No1 level, with the result that the deviations were corrected only after the IP's verbal indications and with delay.

SP, due to degraded situational awareness after the unplanned change of the rejoin sequence, was not cognizant of Aspect Angle and Angle Off during the second straight ahead rejoin. The A/C stabilized at the 15 knot limit and 100 feet from No1 level, with the result that the rejoin was completed only after the IP's verbal indications and the deviation was recognized with delay. Re-establishing awareness of the position within the formation before each rejoin is expected.

SP, due to a late crosscheck of the closure rate against the No1 wingline, did not achieve stabilization in route position on the first attempt of the straight ahead rejoin. The residual overtake produced 10 knots of excess airspeed and 65 feet above No1 level, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on the rejoin line, did not keep the Angle Off constant during the closure on the straight ahead rejoin. The A/C arrived in route position 9 knots fast and 60 feet above No1 level, with the deviations recognized and corrected in a timely manner without the IP's intervention. Visual on No1 was maintained throughout.

SP executed the straight ahead rejoin accurately and with adequate speed according to the Techniques and Procedures Manual, reaching route position within 5 knots of airspeed and 45 feet of No1 level. However, the closure required two power corrections on each of the three rejoins and the straight ahead tactical rejoin was flown at the wide limit of the briefed geometry. Marginal performance for the Training Section; a single, correctly timed power reduction based on Aspect Angle is expected on the next sortie.

SP flew the straight ahead rejoin and the straight ahead tactical rejoin with exceptional precision, controlling the A/C in a smooth and solid manner and remaining cognizant of Aspect Angle and Angle Off at every stage of the closure. Visual on No1 was continuous and route position was held within 2 knots of airspeed and 10 feet of No1 level, above the desired levels for the Training Section. Above end of block MIF achieved.
